cards.text: This is a psalm of David, for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments, and David opens by praying straight to God. Listen to my prayer, don't ignore my plea, attend to me, answer me. That's four ways of saying HEAR ME, friend, and that is NOT a man who sends one polite text and goes to bed.

cards.question: David says he's restless in his complaint and distraught. What has him so shaken up?

cards.text: The wicked are pressing in, bringing disaster down on David and resenting him in their anger. You've had a bad week, friend, but David is having a bad PSALM.

cards.question: True or false: through all this pressure from the wicked, David says his heart stays calm.

cards.text: His heart pounds, the terrors of death assail him, fear and trembling grip him, and horror has overwhelmed him. My heart did that every single time the junk drawer rattled open, and friend, I'm a cookie stamper. I don't even HAVE a heart.

cards.question: When it all gets to be too much, David wishes he had something. What does he wish for?
With wings like a dove, David says he would fly away and find ___.

cards.text: Wings like a dove! My little Minty would be SO proud right now. David says, "How far away I would flee!" and friend, that's the I'm-quitting-selling-everything-and-moving-off-the-grid speech every tired adult has given at least once.

cards.question: If David could fly off, he says he'd flee far away and remain in the ___.

cards.text: David says he'd hurry to his shelter, far from this raging tempest. No forwarding address, no phone, just GONE.

cards.question: David wants to get far away from this raging tempest. What is he really talking about?

answers.text: Everything the wicked are doing to him
A storm coming in off the sea
A long season with no rain

cards.text: Then David stops dreaming about wings and starts praying again. He asks the Lord to confuse and confound their speech.

cards.question: Why does David ask the Lord to confuse and confound their speech?

answers.text: He sees violence and strife in the city
They have been worshiping other gods
They refused to pay the temple tax

cards.text: And this city is not quiet. Day and night, they encircle the walls.

cards.question: True or false: David says that whatever is circling outside the walls, the streets inside the city are safe.

cards.text: Nope. Malice and trouble lie within, destruction is within, and oppression and deceit never leave the streets. That's a city where you lock the door, check the lock, and then lie awake checking it AGAIN in your head.
Then David says what's really cutting him. It isn't an enemy insulting him, because that he could endure, and it isn't a foe rising against him, because from him he could hide.

cards.question: The one rising against David is a man like himself, his companion and close ___.

cards.text: His close FRIEND, the one he shared sweet fellowship with. An enemy, David can take, but your buddy from the group chat turning on you? That one sits on your chest for a while.

cards.question: True or false: David and this close friend used to walk with the crowd into the house of God together.

cards.text: And David is not holding back. He says, "Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes."

cards.question: Then David turns. With trouble this close to home, what does David do?

cards.text: "But I call to God, and the LORD saves me." Morning, noon, and night David cries out in distress, which is more check-ins than I give a tray in the oven, and I hover over THAT tray like it owes me money.

cards.question: True or false: David says God gets tired of hearing him cry out morning, noon and night.

cards.text: God hears him every time. "He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me."

cards.question: David says God, the One enthroned for the ages, will hear and humiliate the people against him. Why?

answers.text: They don't change and have no fear of God
They don't keep the Sabbath day holy
They don't bring offerings to the temple

cards.text: Then David says it plain: "My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant."

cards.question: David says this companion's speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. What does David mean?

answers.text: His words sound kind but he means harm
His words sound harsh but he means well
His words are true but he rarely speaks

cards.text: "His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed." You know this guy: he says "I LOVE that idea!" in the meeting, then walks into the boss's office and calls it HIS idea.

cards.question: Then David says what to do with a burden. Where does he say to cast it?

cards.text: "Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you." CAST it, friend, not hand it over and keep one hand on it, which is exactly how I held onto my troubles in that drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD will let the righteous be shaken now and then.

cards.text: And the wicked? "But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days."

cards.question: After all of it, the fear, the violent city and the friend who turned, David ends with this: "But I will ___ in You."
